habitat: Mountainous terrain of the Tibetan plateau; cliffs; rocky ledges; at 600–4500 m
story: In the diverse world of birds, the Himalayan Vulture (Gyps himalayensis) stands out. This species, part of the Accipitridae family, is a resident of Mountainous terrain of the Tibetan plateau; cliffs; rocky ledges; at 600–4500 m. Its IUCN Red List status is Near Threatened (NT), which serves as a call to action for habitat preservation. The Himalayan Vulture is more than just a bird; it is a symbol of the rich biodiversity that we must protect. Through this poster, we hope to foster a greater understanding and appreciation for the Himalayan Vulture and its role in the ecosystem.
Every poster is crafted to inspire curiosity about our planet's incredible biodiversity.
